story_type: sailboat trapped in Arctic ice, polar icebreaker tows it out
hook: His sailboat got trapped in Arctic ice, 40 miles off Alaska.
narration: This sailboat was trapped in Arctic ice, about forty miles off Barrow, Alaska.
He was trying to sail the Northwest Passage, Vancouver to eastern Canada.
Search and rescue on Alaska's North Slope called the Coast Guard.
Help came from the Healy, a polar icebreaker out on a science mission.
An icebreaker rides up onto the ice and crushes it under its own weight, leaving open water behind it.
outcome: The Healy crew rescued him, and towed his boat through the ice behind them.
title: Sailboat trapped in Arctic ice
description:
On July 12, 2014, the crew of the Coast Guard Cutter Healy, a polar icebreaker on a research mission, rescued a man aboard a 36-foot sailboat trapped in Arctic ice about 40 miles northeast of Barrow, Alaska. He was sailing from Vancouver to eastern Canada through the Northwest Passage.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video courtesy of Coast Guard Cutter Healy, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/349177/coast-guard-icebreaker-rescues-man-aboard-sailboat-trapped-arctic-ice
